kit.name: ELEGOO UNO R3 Project Most Complete Starter Kit

identity.manufacturer: unbranded / generic (no manufacturer markings printed on the part)
identity.manufacturer_part_number: not specified by ELEGOO, generic part; comparable retail part is Adafruit product 2195
generic_equivalents: Adafruit 10uF 50V electrolytic capacitor, product 2195, sold as a 10-pack
identity.package: radial through-hole electrolytic can, about 5mm diameter x 12mm tall (per Adafruit's comparable part)

function.one_sentence_plain_english: A small can-shaped capacitor that stores much more charge than a ceramic capacitor and smooths out slower power dips, but only works if wired the correct way around.
function.what_it_is_used_for: Filtering and smoothing power-supply ripple or voltage dips, for example after a voltage regulator or near a part that pulls current in short bursts.
function.how_it_works_briefly: Like the ceramic capacitors in this kit, it stores charge on two plates, but the plates are rolled up with a chemical electrolyte between them, letting it hold roughly 100,000 times more charge than the kit's 22pF ceramic capacitor in a similar-sized package. That chemical construction is also why it only works with current flowing one direction; it is polarized.

pinout.name: positive lead (anode)
pinout.notes: the longer of the two leads

pinout.name: negative lead (cathode)
pinout.notes: the shorter lead, on the side marked with a printed stripe down the can

pins.pin_1_identification: The longer lead is positive. The lead next to the printed stripe on the side of the can is negative.

electrical.typical_current: not applicable, passive component with no intrinsic current draw

key_specs.tolerance_percent: approximately +/-20%, typical for this class of general-purpose electrolytic capacitor per Adafruit product 2195; ELEGOO's exact tolerance is not independently confirmed
key_specs.case_size: about 5mm diameter x 12mm tall body, positive lead extends to about 25mm total, per Adafruit product 2195
key_specs.polarity: positive lead longer; negative side marked with a printed stripe

visual_identification.shape_and_size: A small cylindrical 'can', noticeably fatter and taller than either ceramic disc capacitor in this kit, roughly the size of a pencil eraser or smaller.
visual_identification.color_and_markings: Body usually black or dark blue, with white printed text showing the capacitance and voltage directly on the can (for example '10uF 50V'). A pale stripe runs down one side marking the negative lead.
visual_identification.printed_text_to_look_for: 10uF, 50V, printed directly rather than as a 3-digit code
easily_confused_with: 100uF electrolytic capacitor: same cylindrical shape and stripe marking, but a visibly larger body and a different printed value
other small electrolytic capacitors of different voltage or capacitance rating, distinguished by the printed text

hazards: installing it backwards (reverse polarity) or exceeding its 50V rating can cause it to heat up, bulge, vent, or in rare cases pop
do not touch a hot or visibly bulging capacitor
handling_notes: always check the negative stripe before powering the circuit
bend leads gently, not sharply right at the body, to avoid cracking the internal seal
common_mistakes: confusing it with the visually similar but larger 100uF capacitor and using the wrong value

symptoms_and_causes.symptom: capacitor feels warm, the top bulges, or there is a small pop or hiss
symptoms_and_causes.likely_cause: installed backwards or exposed to more than 50V
symptoms_and_causes.check: power off immediately, verify orientation against the negative stripe, and replace the part if the top is domed or leaking

symptoms_and_causes.symptom: circuit does not get the expected power smoothing
symptoms_and_causes.likely_cause: capacitor installed backwards, a bad solder or breadboard connection, or the wrong part substituted
symptoms_and_causes.check: use a multimeter's capacitance mode; expect a reading close to 10uF, and check continuity of both leads

troubleshooting.how_to_test_with_a_multimeter: Discharge the capacitor first by briefly connecting a resistor across its leads, then set the multimeter to capacitance mode; expect a reading close to 10uF. Do not test an electrolytic on a diode or continuity setting expecting a simple short or open reading, since it will show a brief charging blip instead.

ELEGOO's own website (elegoo.com and us.elegoo.com product/tutorial pages) returned HTTP 403 Forbidden on every fetch attempt, so this record relies on a third-party retailer listing and a third-party host of ELEGOO's own instruction manual instead. ELEGOO ships a generic, unbranded part and publishes no datasheet, manufacturer name, or MPN for it. market.unit_price_usd is computed by dividing Adafruit's comparable 10-pack price ($1.95) by 10, not a confirmed ELEGOO or single-unit retail price.
